questions.question: On a 1:50 000 map, one centimetre on the paper represents:
options: 50 000 centimetres of ground, which is 500 metres — half a kilometre

questions.question: The three forms in which scale appears on a topographic sheet are:
options: Ratio, contour interval and grid reference
Word scale, ratio scale and linear scale bar
North arrow, ratio and margin note

questions.question: Comparing 1:10 000 and 1:50 000, the 1:10 000 map is:
options: The smaller scale, showing more ground
The same scale in different units
The larger scale, showing a smaller area in more detail

questions.question: The formula line for converting a map measurement to ground distance is:
options: Real distance = map distance divided by the scale factor
Real distance = map distance plus the scale factor
Real distance = scale factor divided by map distance
Real distance = map distance multiplied by the scale factor

questions.question: 7,4 cm multiplied by 50 000 gives:
Walking 370 000 cm down the unit ladder gives:
On a 1:50 000 sheet, a measuring error of one millimetre equals a ground error of about:
To measure a winding road on a map, you should:
options: Lay string or a pivoted paper edge along the curves, then straighten it against a ruler
Use a rigid ruler corner to corner
Estimate by eye and double it
Count the contour lines it crosses

questions.question: The same 7,4 cm measured on a 1:10 000 orthophoto represents:
Given a real distance of 3,7 km, the separation on a 1:50 000 map is found by:
options: Converting to 370 000 cm and dividing by 50 000, giving 7,4 cm

subtopics.title: Verification, Error Traps and Where This Skill Feeds

questions.question: The hand-span sense check on a 1:50 000 sheet works because a span of about 10 cm covers roughly:
options: Five kilometres — about an hour's walk

questions.question: On the unit ladder, centimetres become metres by:
Rounding 7,4 cm to 7,5 cm before multiplying at 1:50 000 builds in a ground error of about:
Which later calculation does NOT consume the scale-and-distance conversion?
options: Gradient, which needs horizontal ground distance
Area, which multiplies two converted distances
Cross-sections, which need distances along the section line
Identifying the season on a synoptic chart

subtopics.title: The District, Shrunk Fifty Thousand Times

questions.question: In the scale-model picture, the one thing you need to know about any map is:
options: How hard it was shrunk — the shrink factor printed on the sheet
What paper it is printed on

questions.question: The marinade recipe of one part sauce to five parts water shows that a ratio:
options: Compares rather than counts, so it works in any unit — spoons or jugs, centimetres or millimetres
Must always be converted to litres first

questions.question: The printed bar along the bottom margin of the sheet lets you:
options: Step a distance off with a paper edge and read kilometres with no arithmetic

questions.question: In the maps-app zoom picture, the 1:10 000 orthophoto is:
options: The zoomed-out view showing the whole province
The same zoom as the topographic sheet
A view with no scale at all
The zoomed-in view — larger scale, small area, rich detail

subtopics.title: Multiply Once, Then Step Down Twice

questions.question: Taking 7,4 × 50 000 in two bites gives:
The two steps down the ladder from 370 000 cm are:
options: Divide by 1 000 to metres, then by 100 to kilometres
Divide by 100 to get 3 700 m, then by 1 000 to get 3,7 km

questions.question: The word 'kilometres' at the end of the answer matters because:
options: A number without its unit is an incomplete answer, and the unit often carries its own mark
It proves you used a calculator

questions.question: The halving shortcut on a 1:50 000 sheet should be used:
options: As a check, while the full method is written out, because halving works only at this one scale

subtopics.title: Shoelaces, Zoomed-in Sheets and the Hand-Span Test

questions.question: A shoelace pressed along a winding route reads 11,8 cm on a 1:50 000 sheet. The real distance is:
The same paper distance covers one fifth of the ground on the orthophoto because:
options: Its shrink factor is 10 000 instead of 50 000 — it is the zoomed-in sheet
The topographic sheet is more accurate

questions.question: Running the machine backwards — ground to map — you:
options: Divide by the scale factor: 370 000 cm ÷ 50 000 = 7,4 cm

questions.question: An answer of 37 km for a measurement under one hand-span fails the sense check because:
options: 37 km is always wrong on any map
A hand-span on a 1:50 000 sheet is only about 5 km, so a decimal must have slipped
